findings.title: Migration crashes when no embed_category setting row exists
findings.body: The query joining `categories` to `site_settings` on `name = 'embed_category'` returns no rows when `embed_category` was never set. That is the default (`''` is not persisted), it is the state on every fresh install, and it also happens when the stored name no longer matches a category. Calling `[0]` on an empty PG::Result raises IndexError (and even if it returned nil, `['id']` would raise NoMethodError). So `rake db:migrate` aborts for most existing sites and all new installs. The `category_id == 0` fallback is never reached. Check `ntuples`/`cmd_tuples` before indexing.

findings.title: Migrated hosts are not normalized, silently breaking existing embeds
findings.body:
The old `allows_embeddable_host?` explicitly accepted entries like `http://eviltrout.com` and `https://...`; there were specs for this. The migration inserts each line of `embeddable_hosts` verbatim. It does not strip the scheme, path, whitespace or `\r` (CRLF input), and it does not skip blank lines.

The new lookup compares `lower(host)` against the bare `uri.host`. Rows such as `http://eviltrout.com` or `eviltrout.com\r` therefore never match. After upgrading, those sites get `InvalidAccess` on every embed request and TopicRetriever stops importing. Hosts should be normalized the same way the model's `before_validation` does, or inserted via the model.

findings.title: Raw string interpolation into INSERT SQL
findings.body: Each host value is interpolated directly into `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` without quoting or escaping. Any stored value containing a single quote makes the migration fail with a SQL syntax error, and in general this is an injection-prone pattern. Use `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)` or bind parameters.

findings.title: before_validation crashes with NoMethodError when host is nil
findings.body: `self.host.sub!(...)` is called unconditionally. When `host` is nil, `valid?`/`save` raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error. This happens for `EmbeddableHost.new` without a host, or when the admin controller receives a request without `embeddable_host[host]`; the result is a 500 error. Guard with `if host.present?` (and add a presence validation).

findings.title: Case-insensitive lookup only lowercases one side
findings.body: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases the stored column but not the input. Ruby's `URI#host` preserves case, so a referer or `embed_url` with uppercase letters (e.g. `http://EvilTrout.com/...`, which can come from the user-supplied `embed_url` param to TopicRetriever) will never match. Use `host.downcase` for the bound value.

findings.title: Host format validation rejects valid TLDs longer than 5 characters
findings.body: The regex requires the TLD to match `[a-z]{2,5}`. This rejects many real domains such as `.museum`, `.travel`, `.digital` and `.technology`, as well as `localhost` and IP addresses. Admins cannot add these hosts through the new UI, although the previous free-form site setting accepted them. Hosts migrated via raw SQL in that format can never be edited and re-saved either.

findings.title: Hosts saved with a port can never match
findings.body: The validation explicitly allows an optional `:port`, and `before_validation` only strips the scheme and path, so `example.com:8080` is stored as is. `record_for_host` compares against `URI#host`, which never includes the port. Such a record is accepted by the UI but never authorizes any referer.

findings.title: update/destroy raise 500 for unknown ids
findings.body: Both `update` and `destroy` use `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`, which returns nil for a missing id. `save_host(nil)` / `host.destroy` then raise NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of a 404. This happens with a stale UI or a double-delete. Use `find` or raise `Discourse::NotFound` when the record is nil.

findings.title: Category badge is cleared when no category is chosen
findings.body: When the admin saves without choosing a category, `categoryId` is null. The server substitutes `uncategorized_category_id`, but the client sets `host.category` to `Discourse.Category.findById(null)`, which is undefined. The row shows no category until the page is reloaded. Use the `category_id` returned in the save response instead of the local `categoryId`.

findings.title: Array hydration leaves undefined entries and crashes on null
findings.body: For `*_ids` keys the code maps every id through `_lookupSubType`, which returns undefined when an id is not present in the sideloaded collection. The resulting array can contain undefined holes, so templates that iterate it (e.g. `embeddable-host` components) break. If the value is null, `obj[k].map` throws. The `hydrated || []` fallback does nothing because `map` always returns an array. Filter out missing entries and guard against non-array values.

findings.title: find-embedded test passes only because the fixture ignores the id
findings.body: The test fetches `store.find('fruit', 2)` (banana, `color_ids: [3]`) but asserts two colors with ids 1 and 2. It passes only because the Pretender handler for `/fruits/:id` always returns `fruits[0]` (apple). The test does not check what it appears to, and it would fail if the fixture were fixed to respect the id.

findings.title: Test name no longer matches the behavior under test
findings.body: `expandable_first_post?` no longer depends on embeddable hosts at all, since the `embeddable_hosts.present?` check was removed. The spec "is false if embeddable_host is blank" now passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and the topic has no embed. The `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` in the nested before block is irrelevant. The spec gives false confidence about a host-based condition that no longer exists.

findings.title: New admin endpoints have no behavioral tests
findings.body: The specs for `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` and `Admin::EmbeddingController` only assert the class hierarchy. Nothing tests create/update/destroy, the defaulting of `category_id` to uncategorized, validation-error responses, or the serialized embedding payload. The bugs these specs would catch (nil handling, missing records) go undetected.

findings.title: Fabricator definitions are in each other's files
findings.body: `category_fabricator.rb` now defines only `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, and the new `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` holds all the category fabricators. It works because every fabricator file is loaded, but anyone looking for the category fabricators in `category_fabricator.rb` won't find them. The two files' contents should be swapped.

findings.title: No integrity between embeddable hosts and categories; duplicates allowed
findings.body:
`category_id` is NOT NULL, but there is no foreign key, no validation that the category exists, and no cleanup when a category is deleted. Hosts can end up pointing at nonexistent categories: the admin UI badge is blank and imports silently go to uncategorized.

There is also no uniqueness validation or index on `host`. Duplicate rows can be created, and `record_for_host` then picks an arbitrary one with `.first`, making the target category nondeterministic.
